chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umair and Abu Ali Al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever performs an evil deed is respited regarding it for seven hours of the day. So if he says, 'I seek Forgiveness of Allah, Who, there is no god except for Him, the Living, the Eternal,' three times, it will not be written against him.

key_terms.لَمْ تُكْتَبْ عَلَيْهِ: it was not written against him

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication and time frame for erasing a sin immediately after it is committed?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlighting the divine mercy of a seven-hour 'grace period' for immediate repentance after a sin. The specific dhikr, 'Astaghfirullaha alladhi la ilaha illa huwa al-hayyu al-qayyum,' leverages the attributes of Life and Self-Subsistence to secure the erasure of the sin from the divine record, emphasizing the efficacy of sincere, timely supplication in Shia jurisprudence.
